items.example_en: I have a headache.
items.note: doler works like gustar: me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies.

items.example_en: Give me your hand.
items.note: Feminine despite the -o ending, and Spanish uses the article, not a possessive.

items.example_en: He broke his arm.
items.note: The reflexive se carries the his.

items.example: Me duelen las piernas después de correr.
items.example_en: My legs hurt after running.

items.example: Me duele la espalda desde ayer.
items.example_en: My back has hurt since yesterday.
items.note: The back of an object is la parte de atrás.

items.example_en: I have a stomach ache.
items.note: la barriga is the informal belly.

items.example_en: I'm hungry, shall we eat something?
items.note: Never estoy hambre. Spanish HAS hunger.

items.example: ¿Tienes sed? Hay agua en la nevera.
items.example_en: Are you thirsty? There's water in the fridge.
I'm cold, can you close the window?
items.note: hace frío is about the weather, tengo frío about you.

items.example: Tengo sueño, me voy a la cama.
items.example_en: I'm sleepy, I'm off to bed.
items.note: el sueño means both sleepiness and a dream.

items.example_en: I need to rest a bit.
items.note: Takes a direct object, no preposition.

items.example_en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?
items.note: In Spain also los servicios or el aseo.

items.example: Desde esta mañana no me encuentro bien.
items.example_en: I haven't been feeling well since this morning.
items.note: Also no me siento bien.

items.example: Tiene fiebre desde hace dos días.
items.example_en: He's had a fever for two days.
items.note: desde hace plus a period covers English for.

items.example: Toso sobre todo por la noche.
items.example_en: I cough mostly at night.
items.note: The noun is la tos.

items.example_en: I have a bit of a cold.
items.note: un resfriado is the cold itself. In Latin America: estar resfriado or agripado.

items.example_en: It hurts here when I press.
How long have you had this pain?
items.note: Answered with desde plus a date, or desde hace plus a duration.

items.example: Quería pedir cita con el médico.
items.example_en: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
items.note: una cita is also a date, romantic or not.

items.example: Aquí tiene su receta para la farmacia.
items.example_en: Here's your prescription for the pharmacy.
items.note: Same word as a cooking recipe.

items.example: Este medicamento se toma después de comer.
items.example_en: This medicine is taken after meals.
items.note: The reflexive se expresses the passive: it is taken.

items.example: Es necesario que descanse tres días.
items.example_en: You need to rest for three days.
items.note: es necesario que triggers the subjunctive: descanse.

items.example_en: We took him to A and E last night.
items.note: Plural. The European emergency number is 112.

items.example_en: Do you have your health card?
items.note: The card that opens the Spanish public health system.

items.example: Hago deporte tres veces por semana.
items.example_en: I exercise three times a week.
items.note: hacer covers most activities: hacer yoga, hacer natación.

items.example_en: I run in the park.
items.note: Regular -er verb, unlike its French cousin.

items.example_en: I've signed up at the gym.
items.note: apuntarse a means to sign up for.

items.example_en: She's training for a marathon.
You look in great shape!

items.example: Tengo agujetas por todo el cuerpo.
items.example_en: I ache all over.
items.note: The specific word for post-exercise muscle soreness.

items.example: No he dormido bien esta noche.
items.example_en: I didn't sleep well last night.
items.note: esta noche means both tonight and last night; the tense decides.

items.example_en: Rest, you need it.

items.example: El estrés del trabajo me agota.
items.example_en: Stress at work exhausts me.
items.note: Borrowed from English, with a Spanish e- in front of the s.

items.example: El fin de semana intento relajarme.
items.example_en: At the weekend I try to relax.
items.note: The pronoun attaches to the infinitive: relajarme.

items.example_en: You have to look after yourself in winter.
See you soon. Take care!
items.note: A warm way to end a call or a message.
